minutes.headline: Select Board delegated approval of a letter backing an MBTA Communities planning grant; no budget decisions made.
minutes.summary: The Select Board ratified annual town manager and police appointments, approved prior minutes and a warrant, and heard a long town manager report on 30 School Street, Ritter and Town Hall alterations, records retention and email migration. A student's geocaching project was settled, a draft town manager evaluation was entered, and the board authorized the chair and town manager to approve a letter of support for an MBTA Communities planning assistance grant. A member also reported on the municipal building design committee's joint meeting with the School Committee.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to let the chair and town manager approve a letter supporting a regional planning grant for MBTA Communities compliance.
The board ratified the town manager's annual appointments and the list of police officers for reappointment effective July 1, 2022; both passed.
The town manager reported on 30 School Street, where a state-funded asbestos project is complete and further abatement and a demolition estimate follow.
The board entered a draft town manager evaluation, with members to send changes to the chair and finalization planned for next week.
The board considered an accounts payable warrant; the vote outcome is not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: The grant is described as free and state-funded through fiscal year 24 and as not obliging the town to adopt zoning, so it bears on how Lunenburg plans for MBTA Communities rules without a town appropriation.
The 30 School Street work and the records retention plan are capital items that could shape future capital requests and the cost of building space.
watch_next: Finalization of the town manager evaluation, expected at the board's next week meeting.
The estimate for demolition and remaining hazardous materials abatement at 30 School Street.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the main votes (annual appointments, police reappointments, MRPC grant letter) and on the $50,000 and $334,176.53 figures. They differ on the accounts payable warrant, which ours lists as an inaudible vote and the town records as the Board signing it. Ours also holds several items the official text lacks (geocache, tree, volunteer event, $200,000 MassDevelopment figure, storage space), and the official text has the pole petitions and the building-naming policy.
